title: Keep a cancelled booking's refund for the client's next booking
who: Any staff. A manager to undo it.
summary: A booking was cancelled and we owe the client money back, but they would rather we kept it for when they rebook.
useWhen: The job is Cancelled and its cancellation fee has been invoiced and paid.
The invoice panel says there is money "to refund to the client".
The client has asked us to keep it for a future booking.

notWhen.text: The client wants the money back. Use Process on the pending refund instead.
The cancellation fee has not been invoiced yet. A manager raises the fee invoice first.

steps.text: Open the cancelled job and go to its Money tab.
steps.detail: The panel is titled Cancellation fee and says "Refund due", with the amount to refund.
It is on the amber "to refund to the client" line.

steps.text: Add a note saying why, then press Hold on account again.
steps.detail: For example who asked, and roughly when they expect to rebook.

steps.text: Check the panel now says Settled, with the money held.
steps.detail: The pending refund on this job has been cleared, marked "Held on account for their next booking".

steps.text: When they rebook, use it on the new job.
steps.detail: It shows in the new job's Client History panel like any other money on account.

next: Nothing has moved. The money is still on the cancelled job's payments in HireHop and Xero.
The job drops off Owed to Clients in Money > Overview and appears under Held on Account instead.
The cancelled job stays Cancelled. It is never completed.

wrong.problem: There is no Hold on account button.
wrong.fix: The cancellation fee has to be invoiced and paid first. If the panel says "Fee to invoice", a manager presses Raise fee invoice.

wrong.problem: The client changed their mind and wants the refund after all.
wrong.fix: A manager opens the ... menu at the top right of the panel and chooses Stop holding on account. The pending refund comes back and can be processed as normal.
It stays in Money > Overview, Held on Account, with how long it has been there. Either refund it from the cancelled job or keep holding; it does not expire.
